Execution order: step 10 of 13. Depends on Adashi task ID 19. Complete this prerequisite before starting.

Phase: shared server SQL design, after the SQLite and Git-friendly phases.

Select and document the initial supported server SQL engine and deployment/access model before implementation:
- Preserve one logical store and backend selection per project; define project isolation even when a server hosts several projects.
- Decide connection ownership, connection pooling, network timeouts, cancellation, schema migration ownership and supported client/schema compatibility.
- Define user identity, authentication, project permissions and attribution. Do not confuse a computer ID or local alias with an authenticated user; enforce authorization at the selected trusted boundary.
- Define secure connection/secret references, TLS verification, credential rotation and safe logs. Shareable project metadata must not contain passwords or tokens.
- Map the common adapter contract to SQL transactions, resource-version/readToken checks, operation receipts, reference integrity and external-change detection.
- Specify concurrent edits, deletion conflicts, disconnects, ambiguous commit outcomes and retries. Reconnection must not duplicate committed mutations or create a divergent local fallback.
- Specify backup/restore and upgrades, and the location/trust policy for executing shared QA definitions; sharing a database must not implicitly execute another user's commands.

Acceptance: formal architecture and sequence diagrams settle the engine, trust boundary, project/user model, failure semantics and migration strategy while preserving the shared desktop/MCP adapter. Record remaining product choices explicitly.

Markdown design artefact integration (approved 2026-09-25):
The shared domain now explicitly includes the approved Markdown design requirements on storage-server-sql, storage-core and store-design-workspace. Coordinate the SQL design with Markdown 01/12 (task ID 25); do not freeze a server schema/API that omits this domain. Define full-body storage, stable external/portable identities, ordered design associations, direct bindings, task/QA links, search/backlinks, snapshot readTokens, atomic delete/reference protection and authenticated authoring. Generated .md files remain per-checkout projections and are never another SQL write source. Include document conflict/retry and backup/restore behavior in the engine/trust-boundary design.

data.title: Storage 10/13 — Design shared server SQL storage and multi-user access
